captions.instagram:
How does an induction stove work?

The glass stays cool, yet the pan boils water in three minutes. Take an induction hob apart in 3D, watch eddy currents crowd into a skin thinner than a hair, and race it against gas and an electric coil.

→ Under the glass of an induction hob: a flat copper coil, ferrite bars and a box of fast electronics.
→ The coil’s field flips 24,000 times a second and drives eddy currents round inside the pan’s base.
→ Swap in aluminium and the same current makes about 1% of the heat. The hob refuses to start.
→ Rectify the 50 Hz mains to DC, then chop it back into AC at about 30,000 times a second.
→ No pan? A test pulse rings on and on, so the hob stays off.

youtubeLong.title: How does an induction stove work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
The glass stays cool, yet the pan boils water in three minutes. Take an induction hob apart in 3D, watch eddy currents crowd into a skin thinner than a hair, and race it against gas and an electric coil.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/inductionclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/inductionclear

In this video:
• A coil under glass, not a heater. Under the black glass-ceramic top sits a flat spiral coil of Litz wire with ferrite bars below it, and a board of power electronics: a rectifier, two IGBT switches on a heat sink, a capacitor and a fan.
• The pan is the heater. The coil's current swings back and forth about 24,000 times a second.
• Why it needs a magnetic pan. At these frequencies the current crowds into a thin skin: about 0.23 mm in cast iron, 0.53 mm in aluminium.
• Electronics tuned like a swing. A rectifier turns the 230 V mains into DC of up to 325 V, and two IGBTs chop it into fast AC through the coil and a capacitor.
• Less waste on the way to the pot. Boiling 1 litre from 25 °C needs 314 kJ whatever the stove.
• A 2 kW load and a fast pan. At 2,000 W the hob draws 8.7 A, so it needs a 16 A wall socket, not a thin extension board.
